def wide():

distilled = F.kl_div(

A small source-reading fixture for MLView. Do not run it: the dataset and
checkpoint are deliberately external. The selected scenario is
`configs/distill.json`, passed to `train.py` with `--config`.

It exercises configuration-selected construction, a frozen teacher, two loss

findings.message: external/teacher.pt is not in the workspace and no code here creates it. The run strict-loads it into the wide architecture and then puts 60% of the loss weight on matching its softened outputs, so both a successful start (a bare state_dict with keys and shapes for Linear(10,64) - ReLU - Linear(64,3)) and the value of distillation (a teacher that is actually accurate on this task's 3 classes) depend on facts that cannot be established from source. The teacher is also never evaluated on the validation set, so a weak or mismatched teacher would not be revealed by this script's output.
findings.suggestion: Before running, confirm the file is a state_dict with 0.weight [64,10], 0.bias [64], 2.weight [3,64], 2.bias [3], record how the teacher was trained, and measure the teacher once on the validation batches (evaluate() accepts any module) so the student's accuracy has a reference point.
findings.title: Teacher checkpoint is external: compatibility and quality cannot be verified

nodes.detail: json.load() yields a plain dict that run() indexes with config[...]. There are no defaults, schema checks, or merging, so all ten keys are required and all ten are consumed: student=small, teacher=wide, teacher_checkpoint=external/teacher.pt, train_data=external/train.pt, validation_data=external/validation.pt, alpha=0.6, temperature=2.0, learning_rate=0.001, epochs=5, output=student.pt. Batch size (32), optimizer type (Adam) and CPU map_location are hard-coded in train.py rather than configured.
nodes.label: Load distill.json into a dict and call run(config)

nodes.detail: models.build(name) performs BUILDERS[name]() - a dict lookup followed by a zero-argument call, which is why construction is driven by the config string rather than a fixed call name. The registry has exactly two entries, small and wide; any other name raises KeyError. Each call returns a fresh, randomly initialised nn.Sequential; no seed is set anywhere in the inspected source.
nodes.label: Model registry: BUILDERS name -> constructor

nodes.detail: config["student"] is "small", so BUILDERS["small"] resolves to small(): 10 input features, one 16-unit hidden layer, 3 class logits (10*16+16 + 16*3+3 = 227 parameters). The student starts from random initialisation; this entrypoint never loads a student checkpoint. It is the only module handed to the optimizer and the only module saved.
nodes.label: Student = build("small") -> Linear(10,16) - ReLU - Linear(16,3)

nodes.detail: config["teacher"] is "wide", so BUILDERS["wide"] resolves to wide(): the same 10-feature input and 3-logit output as the student but a 64-unit hidden layer (10*64+64 + 64*3+3 = 899 parameters). The architectures differ, but the matching 3-logit outputs are what make the per-class KL term well defined.
nodes.label: Teacher = build("wide") -> Linear(10,64) - ReLU - Linear(64,3)

Unknown: whether it exists at launch; how, and on what data, the teacher was trained; its accuracy; and whether its state_dict keys and shapes match wide() (expected for that Sequential: 0.weight [64,10], 0.bias [64], 2.weight [3,64], 2.bias [3]). The relative path resolves against the launch cwd, which is also unrecorded.
nodes.label: external/teacher.pt - teacher checkpoint (not in workspace)

nodes.detail: torch.load(..., map_location="cpu", weights_only=True) deserialises tensors only, onto CPU. load_state_dict is called without strict=False, so PyTorch's default strict matching applies: the file must be a bare state_dict for the wide architecture. A wrapped dict (for example {"model": ...}) or a differently shaped teacher would raise at this line, before any training happens.
nodes.label: Load teacher weights from the checkpoint

nodes.detail: All teacher parameters are marked non-trainable immediately after loading. This is the first of three independent guards: (1) requires_grad_(False) here; (2) teacher.eval() plus torch.no_grad() around the teacher forward inside train_epoch; (3) the optimizer is built from student.parameters() only. Counter-evidence search over all inspected files: no later requires_grad_(True), no second optimizer, and the teacher is never saved - nothing in the source can modify teacher weights.
nodes.label: Freeze teacher: requires_grad_(False)

nodes.detail: The only optimizer in the run. Its parameter list is the student's parameters; the teacher is never registered, so optimizer.step() cannot touch it. Apart from lr=config["learning_rate"]=0.001 Adam uses library defaults; there is no scheduler, weight decay, or gradient clipping in the inspected source.
nodes.label: Adam(student.parameters(), lr=0.001)

nodes.detail: Shared helper used for both splits. It expects the file to deserialise (weights_only=True, CPU) to a mapping with tensor entries "features" and "labels", wraps them in a TensorDataset, and returns a DataLoader with hard-coded batch_size=32 and the caller's shuffle flag. drop_last is not set, so a final short batch is kept. No transforms, normalisation, or augmentation are applied.
nodes.label: batches(): torch.load -> TensorDataset -> DataLoader(batch_size=32)

nodes.detail: Only the path and the two required keys are known. Unknown: sample count, feature dtype and scale, label dtype and class balance, and provenance. The code implies features must be [N,10] floats (the first Linear takes 10 inputs) and labels [N] integer class ids in 0..2 (cross_entropy over 3 logits), but nothing in the workspace confirms the file meets that contract.
nodes.label: external/train.pt - training tensors (not in workspace)

nodes.detail: Same implied contract as the training file ("features" [N,10], "labels" [N] in 0..2). Unknown: size, distribution, and whether it is disjoint from external/train.pt or from whatever data the teacher was trained on. If it holds zero samples, evaluate() returns None rather than an accuracy.
nodes.label: external/validation.pt - validation tensors (not in workspace)

nodes.detail: batches(config["train_data"], shuffle=True): built once before the epoch loop and re-iterated every epoch, so order is reshuffled per epoch. No seed or generator is supplied, so batch order is not reproducible across runs.
nodes.label: Training batches (shuffle=True)

nodes.detail: batches(config["validation_data"], shuffle=False): fixed order, same batch size of 32, built once and reused after every epoch.
nodes.label: Validation batches (shuffle=False)

nodes.detail: for _ in range(config["epochs"]) with epochs=5. Each iteration runs one full train_epoch pass followed by one validation pass. There is no early stopping, scheduler, or break condition: exactly five epochs run unless an exception occurs.
nodes.label: Repeat for 5 epochs

nodes.detail: Called as train_epoch(student, teacher, train_batches, optimizer, config["alpha"], config["temperature"]), i.e. alpha=0.6 and temperature=2.0. The function returns nothing and logs nothing: no training loss is reported, so the only runtime signal from the script is the per-epoch validation accuracy.
nodes.label: train_epoch(): one distillation pass over the training batches

nodes.detail: Re-applied at the start of every epoch, which also undoes the student.eval() set by the preceding validation pass. Neither architecture contains dropout or batch-norm, so the modes do not change numerics here, but teacher.eval() is the conventional second guard for a frozen teacher.
nodes.label: student.train(), teacher.eval()

nodes.detail: Iterates the shuffled training DataLoader. Every batch feeds the same features to both networks; labels go only to the supervised term.
nodes.label: For each (features, labels) batch

nodes.detail: teacher_logits = teacher(features) inside a no_grad block, so no autograd graph is recorded for the teacher and its logits act as constant soft targets in the loss.
nodes.label: Teacher forward under torch.no_grad()

nodes.detail: student_logits = student(features) outside the no_grad block: the only grad-tracked computation feeding the loss. The same logits are used by both loss terms.
nodes.label: Student forward (gradients tracked)

nodes.detail: supervised = F.cross_entropy(student_logits, labels): untempered student logits against ground-truth class indices, with the library's default mean reduction.
nodes.label: Loss term 1 - supervised cross-entropy on hard labels

nodes.detail: distilled = F.kl_div(log_softmax(student_logits / T), softmax(teacher_logits / T), reduction="batchmean") * T**2. The input is student log-probabilities and the target is teacher probabilities (log_target is not set), so this is KL(teacher || student) summed over the 3 classes and averaged over the batch. With temperature=2.0 the factor T^2 = 4 restores the gradient magnitude lost by softening - the standard Hinton-style formulation.
nodes.label: Loss term 2 - distillation KL at T=2.0, scaled by T^2

nodes.detail: loss = (1 - alpha) * supervised + alpha * distilled with alpha=0.6: 40% weight on hard-label cross-entropy and 60% on the T^2-scaled distillation term (an effective 0.6 * 4 = 2.4 coefficient on the raw tempered KL).
nodes.label: Total loss = (1 - alpha)*CE + alpha*KD = 0.4*CE + 0.6*KD

nodes.detail: Gradients flow only through student_logits: the teacher logits were produced under no_grad from parameters with requires_grad=False, and the optimizer holds student parameters only. One Adam step per batch; no gradient accumulation or clipping.
nodes.label: zero_grad -> backward -> optimizer.step() (student only)

nodes.detail: Decorated with @torch.no_grad(); sets student.eval(), takes argmax over the logits, counts matches against labels, and returns correct / count - or None when the loader yields no samples. Only the student is evaluated: the teacher's validation accuracy is never measured and no validation loss is computed.
nodes.label: evaluate(): student top-1 accuracy on validation batches

nodes.detail: The metric goes to stdout only. It is not stored, not returned, and not used for early stopping, model selection, or learning-rate control. Its runtime values are unknown because nothing was executed.
nodes.label: print({"validation_accuracy": ...}) once per epoch

nodes.detail: Executed once, after the 5-epoch loop ends. It writes the last-epoch student weights - not the best-validation epoch - as a bare state_dict for the small Sequential. The teacher, optimizer state, epoch counter, config, and metrics are not saved, and there are no intermediate checkpoints. "student.pt" is a relative path, so the file lands in the launch cwd; an existing file of that name would be overwritten.
nodes.label: Save student.state_dict() -> student.pt

nodes.detail: Outside the selected execution path; shown only to explain what the saved checkpoint is compatible with. predict() hard-codes build("small") - it does not read distill.json - then strict-loads a caller-supplied checkpoint path and returns argmax classes. For this config the hard-coded name matches the trained student. That student.pt is the file passed in is an inference: no caller of predict() exists in the workspace.
nodes.label: Separate entrypoint: infer.py predict() (not run by train.py)
